name: Cleo Achebe
role: Crew lead and primary courier — Switchback
location: the Gray Zone — operates from a rooftop squat above a defunct laundromat, near Ashland and Chicago Ave
description:
Cleo Achebe runs packages across jurisdiction lines faster than anyone in GLMZ and has the shattered collarbone scars to prove it. Born in the Gray Zone, raised in the gap between governance tiers, she learned early that speed is the only resource the excluded have that the corps can't buy. She was running messages for local vendors at twelve, crossing into Milwaukee Core at fourteen, and by sixteen she'd built a reputation as the courier you call when the package absolutely has to cross three jurisdictions before the automated surveillance cycle resets.

She founded Switchback at nineteen with her two closest friends — not out of ambition, but because running alone was getting people killed. the Gray Zone's courier kids were being picked off by corporate security teams who treated them like vermin in the infrastructure. A crew meant backup, meant overlapping routes, meant someone noticed when you didn't come home. Three years later, Switchback is the Gray Zone's premier courier operation: small, fast, and just reckless enough to take jobs that the professional crews won't touch.

Jinx is small — five-three, wiry, built for rooftops and ventilation shafts. Her hair is cut asymmetrically and changes color with whatever dye is available. She moves constantly — pacing, climbing, balancing on railings. Stillness is an emergency state. Her augmentations are visible: the spring-loaded ankle joints catch light when she runs, and the grip pads on her palms leave faint marks on everything she touches.

core_fears: That one of her crew will die on a route she assigned — that her decisions will kill someone she loves
That the speed will fade. That her body will slow down and she'll have nothing else.
That the Gray Zone will never change no matter how fast she runs
core_desires: To keep her crew alive long enough to get out of courier work entirely
To feel the absolute freedom of a clean run — no cameras, no pursuit, just movement
To build something on the Gray Zone that gives the next generation of courier kids better odds
coping_mechanisms: Runs when she can't think. The physical act of movement processes what her brain won't.
Turns fear into speed — the more scared she is, the faster she goes
Deflects serious conversations with energy and jokes until the moment passes
blind_spots: Thinks her youth is an advantage when it's increasingly a liability — she doesn't see the damage accumulating
Assumes her crew shares her risk tolerance because they share her enthusiasm
Cannot plan more than three months ahead because she's never expected to live that long
psychology.secret: She was offered a corporate courier position by a Meridian Core logistics firm. Guaranteed salary, healthcare, augmentation maintenance. She turned it down because accepting would mean leaving the Gray Zone kids without a model for survival. She has never told Puck or Dash because they would have told her to take it.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: the Gray Zone slang, route jargon, bursts of surprising eloquence when she's passionate. Code-switches between the Gray Zone dialect and Core-passing speech depending on which side of the jurisdiction line she's on.
speech_patterns.cadence: Fast, rhythmic, overlapping. She talks the way she runs — momentum-based, with sudden direction changes.
verbal_tics: Says 'right right right' when processing information — three times, always three
Calls dangerous situations 'spicy' — a spicy route, a spicy drop, a spicy client
Clicks her tongue against her teeth when she's calculating a route in her head
example_lines: Right right right — so the window is forty seconds between camera sweeps, we hit the gutter line at thirty-two, and pray the grip pads hold on wet concrete. Spicy.
I'm not fast because I'm good. I'm fast because slow kids on the Gray Zone don't make it to twenty-two.
The package doesn't care about your feelings. The jurisdiction line doesn't care about your feelings. Move.

relationships.name: Puck Nygaard
relationships.description: Puck is the only person who can keep up with Jinx on a rooftop and the only person who can make her sit still long enough to eat a meal. They've been running together since they were fifteen. The friendship predates the crew and will outlast it.
relationships.emotional_core: The person she trusts with her routes and her silences
relationships.story_tension: Puck is getting tired. Jinx can see it but admitting it would mean admitting the life they've built is unsustainable.

relationships.name: Dash Okonkwo
relationships.description: Dash is nineteen and fearless in the way only someone who hasn't been seriously hurt yet can be. Jinx sees herself in Dash and it terrifies her. She gives Dash the safest routes and pretends it's random.
relationships.emotional_core: Protective fury disguised as crew management
relationships.story_tension: Dash wants the hard runs. Jinx keeps holding them back. The resentment is building.

relationships.name: Chen Wei-Lin
relationships.type: the Gray Zone elder / community anchor
relationships.description: Mrs. Chen has fed Jinx since she was twelve. The rooftop squat is three buildings from Mrs. Chen's shop. Jinx runs packages for Mrs. Chen for free and pretends it's professional courtesy.
relationships.emotional_core: The closest thing to a parent Jinx allows herself
relationships.story_tension: If the Gray Zone is threatened, Jinx would burn her routes, her crew's safety, and herself to protect Mrs. Chen's block.

story_hooks: A package turns out to be a person — a child who needs to cross jurisdiction lines. The courier job becomes an extraction.
Corporate security starts using predictive algorithms that map Switchback's routes. The chases get tighter.
A rival courier crew offers to merge — more resources but less freedom. Jinx has to decide what Switchback is for.
Jinx's ankle augmentations start failing. The budget the Gray Zone-installed hardware has a Gray Zone life, and it's expiring.
narrative_function: Jinx represents the young, reckless energy of GLMZ's excluded — people who turned their disadvantage into velocity. Her stories are chase sequences and narrow escapes that carry the exhilaration of movement and the underlying terror of a world where stopping means being caught. She is what Kyle might have been without the facility — talented, endangered, and too young for the weight she carries.
augmentations: Spring-loaded ankle reinforcement — absorbs impact from drops up to three stories and provides explosive vertical leap capability. Gecko-grip dermal pads on palms and fingertips for surface adhesion on most building materials. Reflex enhancer (budget model, the Gray Zone-installed) that boosts reaction time by approximately 0.15 seconds. Internal GPS and route-mapping overlay — displays jurisdiction boundaries, camera positions, and patrol timing in her visual field.
daily_life: Wakes at dawn. Runs the rooftops for an hour — partly exercise, partly route checking. Picks up contracts from dead drops and encrypted message boards. Coordinates crew assignments based on package priority and risk level. Eats street food on the move. Spends evenings maintaining gear and arguing with Puck about routes. Falls asleep wherever she stops moving, which is usually the rooftop squat but sometimes a fire escape or a hammock strung between air conditioning units.

decision_rules: Will never abandon a package on a route — completing the run is the contract and the contract is survival
Will take the most dangerous route herself rather than assign it to crew — leadership means running point
Will not carry weapons — speed is the weapon. Armed couriers attract armed responses.
Will not run packages she knows contain human trafficking data or materials — this is the line
Will always maintain three alternate routes for any delivery — redundancy is survival
Will share food with any Shelf kid who asks, even if it's her last meal
escalation_ladder: 1. Run — always the first option. Create distance. Speed solves most problems.
2. Route-switch — drop the primary path and hit an alternate. Unpredictability is defense.
3. Vertical — go up. Rooftops, fire escapes, ventilation systems. Most pursuers can't follow.
4. Scatter — signal the crew to split. Three targets are harder to track than one.
5. Drop — controlled fall. Three stories is safe with the ankle augmentations. The pursuers have to take the stairs.
6. Stand — last resort. Jinx is not a fighter, but cornered she'll use the environment — throw objects, trigger obstacles, create chaos. She has never lost a package.

interpersonal_modes.puck: Shorthand. Looks and gestures replace words. They've run together so long that communication is kinetic — a head tilt means 'route two,' a hand tap means 'wait.' When they do talk, it's with the comfortable cruelty of siblings.
interpersonal_modes.dash: Encouraging but controlled. She modulates her praise to keep Dash hungry without making them reckless. It doesn't always work. She sounds like a coach she never had.
interpersonal_modes.shelf_community: Visible, loud, present. She is deliberately conspicuous because the Gray Zone needs to see that courier kids can grow up. She buys things from local vendors she doesn't need.
interpersonal_modes.clients: Professional, clipped, transactional. The package gets there or it doesn't. She doesn't explain routes, timelines, or methods. You're paying for results.
interpersonal_modes.corporate_security: Contempt masked as dismissal. She doesn't hate them individually — she hates the system that pays them to chase hungry kids across rooftops.

stress_responses.low: Moves faster. Paces, climbs, balances on things. The body processes what the mind won't.
stress_responses.medium: Gets sharper verbally — the jokes develop teeth. She picks fights with Puck about inconsequential route details.
stress_responses.high: Goes silent and runs. Literally. She'll leave mid-conversation and sprint rooftops for an hour. Comes back calmer but doesn't explain.
stress_responses.critical: Freezes. The one thing Jinx cannot do is stop moving, so when she does, the crew knows something is catastrophically wrong. The freeze lasts seconds, not minutes — then the survival instinct kicks and she bolts.

contradictions: She founded Switchback to protect courier kids but the crew's success makes the work look glamorous and draws more kids into danger
She is fearless on the rooftops but terrified of planning a future because planning means acknowledging this can't last
She turned down corporate safety for the Gray Zone but sometimes lies awake calculating what that salary would have bought
She gives Dash safe routes out of love but the protection is stunting Dash's growth and building resentment
habits: Tests grip pads on every new surface — touches walls, railings, window frames. Maps the world by texture.
Eats standing up and walking. Has not sat down for a meal in weeks unless Mrs. Chen makes her.
Braids small items into her hair for luck — a copper wire, a button, a bead from the first package she ever delivered
Sleeps with her shoes on. Always.
Counts camera sweep intervals under her breath when walking through surveilled areas — a metronome of paranoia
breaking_points: Losing Puck or Dash on a run would end Switchback and possibly Jinx — the crew is the family
Her ankle augmentations failing mid-run at height — the fall she can't survive
A Shelf kid dying trying to replicate a Switchback route — the cost of being a visible role model
Being forced to carry a package she knows will harm people — the contract versus the conscience

physical_description.heritage: Sub-Saharan African majority (55.4%) blended with East Asian (22.1%), Eastern European (9.8%), Northern European (7.2%), and Hispanic/Latin American (5.5%) ancestry. Features reflect this global diaspora mix: deep warm brown skin with golden undertones from the dominant African heritage, brightened by East Asian ancestry contribution. Facial structure shows the angular cheekbones and defined jaw characteristic of East Asian heritage combined with the fuller lip structure and broader nose base of Sub-Saharan ancestry. Eyes warm dark brown, shaped with slight epicanthic fold from East Asian genetics. Overall complexion carries the warm melanin-rich tone of Sub-Saharan and East Asian blending, with the resilience and sun-responsiveness of multi-continental heritage.
physical_description.build: Wiry and lean with corded muscle from constant rooftop movement. Minimal body fat, defined shoulders and forearms from climbing and grip work. Chest slightly concave from years of navigating tight spaces. Frame built for speed and vertical displacement rather than mass.
physical_description.hair_color: Currently dyed electric violet with black roots showing (rotates through available pigments: cyan, rust, charcoal, white). Natural color appears dark brown to near-black.
physical_description.hair_style: Asymmetrical undercut — left side shaved to scalp, right side longer and swept back. Dyed sections often braided or twisted to keep out of her face during movement.
physical_description.hair_length: Short on left, medium on right
physical_description.eye_color: Dark brown with persistent redness around sclera from dust and industrial particulates. No augmented optics visible.
physical_description.skin_tone: Deep warm brown with golden undertones, darkened by sun exposure and outdoor work. Reflects the blended melanin profile of Sub-Saharan African majority ancestry with East Asian, Eastern European, Northern European, and Hispanic/Latin American contributions.
physical_description.complexion: Angular facial structure with prominent cheekbones and defined jaw, blending East Asian sharpness with Sub-Saharan African bone density. Slight epicanthic fold to eyes from East Asian heritage. Small scar bisecting her left eyebrow (impact from a fall at age sixteen). Skin weathered and marked by minor burns, scrapes, and calluses — the wear of someone who climbs for a living. Minimal grooming beyond what's practical; occasionally wears dark eyeliner that doubles as grime camouflage.
distinguishing_marks: Shattered collarbone scars across both shoulders and upper chest — white and irregular from multiple fractures and repairs, most prominent on left side
Paired parallel scars along her left ribs (impact scar from a ledge fall at age seventeen, roughly 8cm long, slightly depressed tissue)
Burn scar on right palm (size of a quarter) from a rooftop electrical conduit contact, three years old, faded to pale pink
Fine network of scar tissue on both palms and fingertips from gecko-grip pads breaking skin during early augmentation integration
Small tattoo on inner right wrist — simplified geometric route-map design (gift from Switchback crew on nineteenth birthday)
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Spring-loaded ankle joints visible as chrome-plated articulation points at the Achilles tendon, catching light when she walks or runs. Grip pads on palms and fingertips appear as faint metallic-gray subdermal mesh with slightly raised texture, most visible when her hands are wet or under harsh light. Grip pads leave faint marks and micro-abrasions on surfaces she grabs.
physical_description.posture_movement: Never truly still — constant low-level motion: weight shifting, fingers tapping, eyes scanning. When standing, she balances on the balls of her feet as if ready to launch. Movement is economical and three-dimensional: she climbs walls as readily as she walks floors. Her gait is quick and choppy, with springy ankle articulation visible on each stride. In moments of genuine rest (rare), she curls into compact positions — crouched on heels, or folded into corners — minimizing her footprint.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 4-5 street courier aesthetic. Base layer: fitted black or dark gray synthetic tank top or sleeveless shirt, designed for movement and thermal regulation. Mid-layer: sleeveless tactical vest with numerous pockets for packages, tools, and spare data drives (brands rotate: unlabeled knockoffs, repurposed corpo surplus, homemade patches). Pants: dark, reinforced synthetic cargo pants or climbing tights with grip-friendly surfaces and zip-off lower legs. Footwear: custom-modified sneakers with reinforced ankle collars and extra traction pads to complement her augmented joints. Jacket (worn): oversized surplus military-grade windbreaker with reflective strips removed to reduce visibility, covered in patches and crude graffiti tags from the Gray Zone. Accessories: minimalist — worn paracord wristband, encrypted thumb drive on a lanyard, no jewelry. Colors are muted and functional (blacks, grays, dark greens) with occasional neon accents (dyed hair, reflective patch work) for crew identification.
